subject: maki
title: Tree-sitter-bash parse derives permission scopes per command segment; 'allow always' generalizes safely, unparseable commands force a prompt
one_why: `git diff && rm -rf /` yields scopes git+rm (stored as `git *` and `rm *`, never block-wide wildcards -- SHELL_KEYWORDS guards block-openers); parse failure returns the full command with force_prompt=true instead of defaulting allow, inverting the corpus's regex-denylist anti-pattern.

subject: maki
title: Doom-loop breaker deduplicates identical repeated calls instead of aborting the run
one_why: 3 consecutive calls with identical name+input-hash are skipped with an injected error tool-result while the run continues -- gentler than crush's breaker, and the hash+window design is tested as a matrix (tool_dispatch.rs:1142).

subject: maki
title: Embedded monty Python interpreter exposes every tool as an async function, gated by the same dispatcher, with hook-bypass-proof file access
one_why: Filter/transform/pipe happens outside the context window; interpreter `open()` is disabled whenever a plugin hooks `read` so the sandbox cannot route around policy, gather() is re-implemented to keep sibling results on partial failure, and time+memory limits bound the interpreter -- a second code-mode shape (vs codex's v8) that is testable in one binary.

subject: maki
title: Summarizer overflow retry ladder: strip images/thinking, collapse tool results to placeholders, then drop oldest round with orphan cleanup
one_why: Each rung reports whether anything actually shrank so a no-op retry becomes the honest error; provider-413 below the compaction threshold triggers exactly one gauge-consistent compaction per success streak (the gauge's chars/4 floor means threshold can be unmet while the prompt overflows).

subject: maki
title: agent.compact.prepare lets extension layers re-pick which tool results the summarizer sees collapsed; host applies the edit
one_why: Host ships budget-based picks plus capped 4KiB samples, layer returns edited indices, host performs the mutation -- so no layer can orphan a tool call or drop a user message, and domain-aware tools (tests, logs) can spare what a byte budget would wrongly keep; overflow-forced compaction is the one kind a layer cannot skip (:54-56).

subject: maki
title: Loop and compaction tested by scripted StreamResponse replay asserting captured request transcripts; Lua plugin specs run inside the real embedded host
one_why: MockProvider records the exact messages each turn sent, so compaction/carry/recovery semantics are asserted as wire-visible properties; the include-str Lua specs drive all 15 plugin suites through PluginHost in cargo-nextest -- extension layer gets CI coverage against the actual runtime API.

subject: maki
title: Two ephemeral breakpoints walk back over the wire-tail skipping thinking blocks, plus system; no warming
one_why: Standard-but-correct marking (API rejects cache_control on thinking, code walks back to the last cacheable block); absence of pi-style cache warming keeps cache craft one notch below the 8-rung.

subject: maki
title: Deferred MCP tools hidden behind one tool_search catalog entry; a permitted call counts as loading, a denied one loads nothing
one_why: Keeps large MCP surfaces out of every request's tool array while preserving policy ordering -- the tool definition only joins the next request after the permission gate said yes, so probing a denied MCP tool never inflates the prompt.

subject: maki
title: Prompt carries only name+description skill index; bodies load on call; scans rival harness skill dirs
one_why: available_skills block is one sorted `name: description` line each; and project scan includes .claude/skills, .opencode, .agents -- zero-effort migration path for skills written for rival harnesses.

subject: maki
title: Fail-closed prompt path: no response channel means deny, decisions re-checked under the channel lock, and only the answer tagged with this ask's id is consumed
one_why: Headless-with-prompt runs deny instead of hanging or allowing; the double-check closes the rule-changed-while-queued race and ANSWER_ID_SEPARATOR stops a stale answer approving a different ask; every accept/deny emits an otel tool_decision with source attribution (rule/yolo/user_once/session/always/abort).

subject: maki
title: --print --output-format stream-json deliberately Claude-Code-output-compatible, plus stream-json input SDK mode and a full ACP server crate
one_why: Drop-in replacement story is explicit at the wire-format level (README: 'Output is compatible with Claude Code'), and the same agent core serves ACP with elicitation + permission translation -- three host contracts off one event stream.

subject: maki
title: 30s hook-chain deadline resolves to Verdict::Unchanged, so a wedged policy plugin silently stops filtering user messages, stop-gates, and compaction
one_why: cancel.race(hook.run(...)).unwrap_or(Verdict::Unchanged) is documented as UX protection ('past this the loop moves on without it'), but for security-relevant layers (user_message drop/rewrite) the honest alternative is a loud degraded-mode signal or configurable fail-closed; no test pins what happens when the deadline fires.

subject: maki
title: No SECURITY.md and no OS-level sandbox anywhere, but posture claims stay honest
evidence: repo root (no SECURITY.md); grep for seatbelt|bwrap|landlock|seccomp: zero hits; README.md 'Sensible permission system' section
one_why: Approval binding + folder-trust + grammar scopes are real and tested, yet bash runs via plain jobstart; README scopes its 'Sandbox' claim to the interpreter and labels --yolo, without overselling enforcement -- the pi-style honest rung, missing only the SECURITY.md write-up of what does not bind.

subject: maki
title: If an external `rtk` binary is on PATH, every bash command is transparently rewritten through it before execution
one_why: Auto-detect (rtk --version probe) then `rtk rewrite <cmd>` output-compands commands for ~50% bash token savings, but a PATH-planted rtk silently transforms commands before the permission scopes were derived -- scopes come from the original parse, so a rewrite that adds behavior outruns the policy decision; config-disable exists and is documented.

subject: maki
title: Every extension-facing HTTP vets DNS, pins the vetted IP for connect, and re-validates each redirect hop by hand
one_why: Kills the DNS-rebinding TOCTOU ('first lookup vetted the hostname, second could land on 169.254.169.254') by connecting to the vetted address with SNI/Host handling; redirects are followed manually so the guard sees every hop -- the strongest egress guard found outside the sandboxed subjects.
